content:
- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a sharp drop; reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to recognize it; apply slight upward/downward bias based on 3-period moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (especially after sentiment shifts to bullish); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast direction to sentiment trend, not just price history.
